# ataila_order (Data Source)

One order, by id, with its timeline: who placed it, how the quota decided, who approved or rejected it and why, and each step of its delivery. **Read only** (approval stays in the portal). For an AI gateway key order, `key_id` names the key it delivered, never its value. Needs a token holding `orders-read-global` (or `orders-admin-global`) and platform release 1.0.9999 or later.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ataila_order" "chat_key" {
  id = "9b2e4c1d-7a3f-4e5b-8c6d-0f1e2d3c4b5a"
}

# The key the order delivered (never its value), and the order's timeline.
output "delivered_key" {
  value = data.ataila_order.chat_key.key_alias
}

output "timeline" {
  value = [for e in data.ataila_order.chat_key.events : "${e.at} ${e.event} by ${e.actor}"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The order's id (a UUID).

### Read-Only

- `approval_reason` (String) The operator's reason for approving it.
- `approved_at` (String) When it was approved: RFC 3339 in UTC; null if not.
- `approved_by` (String) The operator who approved it; null for an automatic approval or none.
- `catalogue_item_key` (String) The catalogue item ordered (`key` in `ataila_catalogue_items`).
- `catalogue_item_kind` (String) What delivering an order of the item creates: `vdi-desktop`, `project-vm`, `ai-gateway-key`, `project`, `k8s-namespace`, `storage` or `manual` (an operator delivers it by hand).
- `catalogue_item_name` (String) The item's display name.
- `created_at` (String) When it was placed: RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `customer_id` (String) The tenant's customer when the order was placed; null when that customer is gone.
- `dispatch_json` (String) What delivering the order produced, as JSON text (`run_kind`, `run_id`, `key_id`, `key_alias`, `outcome`…); `{}` before delivery starts. Secret-looking members are null.
- `events` (Attributes List) The order's timeline, oldest first: `id`, `at`, `actor` (an e-mail address, or `system:<part>`), `event` and `detail_json`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--events))
- `key_alias` (String) For an AI gateway key order: the alias of the key it delivered. Never the key's value: an order does not hold it.
- `key_id` (String) For an AI gateway key order: the id of the key it delivered (`id` of an `ataila_ai_gateway_key`, which can import it); null otherwise or before delivery.
- `operation_id` (String) The order as an operation, `order:<id>`.
- `overage_json` (String) A one-off overage an operator approved, as JSON text; null when none. It never raised the tenant's quota.
- `project_id` (String) The project the order is for, when its item takes one.
- `quota_check_json` (String) The quota check as recorded on the order, as JSON text: `result`, `decision`, `reasons` and, per dimension, `limit`, `policy`, `allocated`, `reserved`, `requested`, `total`, `remaining` and `result`.
- `quota_decision` (String) The quota check's decision: `auto_approved`, `awaiting_approval` or `refused`.
- `quota_result` (String) The quota check's result: `within`, `over` (the order went to a card) or `refused_hard_cap`.
- `rejected_at` (String) When it was rejected: RFC 3339 in UTC; null if not.
- `rejected_by` (String) The operator who rejected it; null if not.
- `rejection_reason` (String) The operator's reason for rejecting it.
- `requested_by` (String) The member who placed it (`id` of an `ataila_user`); null when that user no longer exists.
- `spec_json` (String) The order form as submitted, as JSON text.
- `status` (String) The order's state: `submitted`, `auto_approved` (within quota, approved by the platform), `awaiting_approval` (on an operator's approval card), `approved`, `rejected`, `dispatched`, `running`, `delivered`, `partial` (delivered in part; an operator can re-run it), `failed` or `cancelled` (withdrawn by the tenant before delivery started).
- `tenant_id` (String) The tenant that placed it.
- `tenant_name` (String) The tenant's display name.
- `updated_at` (String) Its last change: RFC 3339 in UTC.

<a id="nestedatt--events"></a>
### Nested Schema for `events`

Read-Only:

- `actor` (String) Who: an e-mail address, or `system:<part>` when the platform did it.
- `at` (String) When it happened: RFC 3339 in UTC.
- `detail_json` (String) The entry's facts, as JSON text. Secret-looking members are null.
- `event` (String) What happened, e.g. `submitted`, `auto_approved`, `awaiting_approval`, `approved`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `dispatched`, `running`, `delivered`, `partial`, `failed`, `rerun_requested`, `key_revealed`.
- `id` (String) The entry's id; ids grow with time.
